nodes.name: ZnCr2O4 Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: Appropriate amounts of Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and Cr(NO3)3·9H2O (Zn/Cr = 0.5) were dissolved in deionized water to form a metal salt solution. Ammonia solution (6M) and NH4HCO3 (0.075M) were employed as precipitants. The metal salt solution and precipitant were simultaneously added dropwise into a round-bottom flask at 70°C while maintaining a pH of 7. Subsequently, aging was conducted at 90°C for 24 h under a N2 environment with a flow rate of 100 mL/min. The resulting precipitate was collected by filtration and washed multiple times with deionized water to eliminate the mother liquor. Then, it was dried overnight at 110°C; the obtained solids were used as ZnCr2O4 precursors.

nodes.name: Mo-modified ZnCr2O4 Impregnation
nodes.procedure: The Mo-modified ZnCr2O4 samples were prepared using the impregnation method, in which a solution containing H24Mo7N6O24 was added to the ZnCr2O4 precursor as a carrier. Initially, 3g of the ZnCr2O4 precursor was dispersed in a 10 mL deionized water solution, followed by a certain addition of H24Mo7N6O24 and stirring at room temperature for 4 h. Subsequently, the mixture was dried overnight at 110°C and calcined at 450°C for 2 h. Different masses of H24Mo7N6O24 corresponded to varying loadings of Mo on the ZnCr2O4 samples.

nodes.name: nano-HZSM-5 Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: A solution containing 11.2g of tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), 13.1g of tetrapropylammonium hydroxide (TPAOH), 0.3g of aluminum nitrate nonahydrate Al(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.1g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH), 0.1g of isopropanol (IPA), and 2g of urea was prepared by dissolving them in 18.4g of deionized water at room temperature, followed by vigorous stirring for at least 6 h. The resulting suspension was then transferred into a high-pressure stainless reactor lined with PTFE, heated from room temperature to 180°C with a rate of 15°C/h and maintained for 48h to complete the crystallization process. Afterward, the reactor was rapidly cooled using a cold-water bath, followed by filtration to collect the solid material obtained, which was then washed multiple times with deionized water and dried overnight at 90°C for removing the template agent TPAOH. Then, the obtained solid was calcined at 550°C for 5h, acquiring Na-ZSM-5. The aforementioned Na-ZSM-5 zeolite underwent cation exchange treatment through dispersion within a 1M NH4NO3 solution (100 mL) while vigorously stirring for 6h, resulting in conversion from Na-ZSM-5 into NH4-ZSM-5. Finally, NH4-ZSM-5 was further calcined at 550°C for 5h to transform it into the HZSM-5 zeolite powder.

nodes.procedure: The OX-ZEO coupled catalyst was prepared through physical mixing of the metal oxide and zeolite. The catalysts are named S-Mo (1%), S-Mo (4%), B-Mo, and C-Mo according to the Mo loading.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of ZnCr₂O₄ support measured at 167 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ZnCr₂O₄ spinel with a high surface area (167 m²/g, Table S1) serves as the underlying matrix...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images of S-Mo show isolated brighter atomic points identified as Mo single atoms along [311] orientation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The images of S-Mo demonstrated ordered arrays of Zn and Cr atoms along the [311] crystal orientation, with some isolated and brighter atomic points identified as Mo single atoms (Figures 1a and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images of B-Mo reveal binuclear Mo sites as adjacent bright atomic points with distance of about 3.1 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, B-Mo's images (Figures 1b and S3) reveal the presence of binuclear Mo, displayed as several adjacent and bright atomic points with a distance of about 3.1 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM image of C-Mo shows lattice fringe of (110) plane suggesting cluster Mo sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For cluster Mo species (C-Mo), the lattice fringe of the (110) plane was observed on the local surface of the support, suggesting the emergence of cluster Mo sites (Figures 1c and S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious changes of phase structure in S-Mo and B-Mo; C-Mo shows MoO₃ diffraction peaks besides ZnCr₂O₄ spinel phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No obvious changes of phase structure were proposed in XRD patterns of S-Mo and B-Mo, while C-Mo presented the diffraction peaks of MoO₃ besides the ZnCr₂O₄ spinel phase (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge FT k³-weighted EXAFS: S-Mo shows Mo-O (1.88 Å) and Mo-Cr (3.25 Å) indicating isolated Mo-O-Cr sites (Mo-ND=0); B-Mo shows Mo-O (1.91 Å), Mo-Cr (3.20 Å), Mo-Mo (3.47 Å, CN=1.2, Mo-ND=1); C-Mo shows Mo-O (1.96 Å), Mo-Mo (3.25/3.78 Å, CN=4.3, Mo-ND=4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For S-Mo, the first shell peak was fitted with a Mo-O bond coordination (1.88 Å); the scattering at 3.25 Å was attributed to Mo-Cr... For B-Mo, three distinct peaks were observed at 1.91, 3.20, and 3.47 Å... For C-Mo, the first shell is assigned to Mo-O coordination (1.96 Å), the second shell is associated with Mo-Mo (3.25 and 3.78 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES spectra show oxidation states between MoO₂ (+4) and MoO₃ (+6) for S-Mo, B-Mo, and C-Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo K-edges of S-Mo, B-Mo, and C-Mo fall within the range between MoO₂ and MoO₃, exhibiting an oxidation state ranging from +4 to +6.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando DRIFTS during syngas conversion at 390°C shows on S-Mo: formate (1357, 1570, 2870, 2960 cm⁻¹), formaldehyde (1400, 1460, 1518 cm⁻¹), methoxy (1040 cm⁻¹); on B-Mo: enhanced formaldehyde/methoxy peaks plus C-C/C=C/=C-H (1260, 1590, 3071, 3100 cm⁻¹) and CH₂/CH₃ (2877, 2967, 2852, 2963 cm⁻¹) indicating byproducts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando DRIFT spectra for syngas conversion over s-Mo and b-Mo... characteristic bands corresponding to surface species adsorbed on the single-atom Mo surface were observed (Figure S14a and Table S3), including formate (1357, 1570, 2870, 2960 cm⁻¹), formaldehyde (1400, 1460, 1518 cm⁻¹), methoxy groups (1040 cm⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform of k³-weighted EXAFS shows scattering centers for Mo-O, Mo-Cr, Mo-Mo; B-Mo higher intensity than S-Mo at Mo-Mo position, C-Mo highest.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is further confirmed using WT-EXAFS in which the heat maps show two scattering centers that are associated with Mo-O, Mo-Cr, and Mo-Mo (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: H₂-D₂ exchange activation temperature decreases from 380°C (S-Mo) to 285°C (C-Mo) with increasing Mo ND.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The findings... reveal a significant trend: as the ND of the Mo species increases, the temperature required for activation decreases from 380 to 285°C.
